I am  Caucasian and my  ethnicities are Polish, Lithuanian, Irish and English.
Neither my mother nor my aunts had breast cancer.
Section I – Birth through age 10.
Think about potential differences and similarities, including whether your mother smoke or drank alcohol during her pregnancies. Any unusual childhood diseases and/or medications taken. Possible differences in vaccines. Whether either child was born pre-maturely or significantly overweight. Breastfed, Y/N. Physical characteristics/diet preferences/emotional trauma. Neighborhood you grew up in. Outdoor or indoor activities that you liked to engage in. Concerns with environmental contaminants.
I was born in 1953, in the town of Warminster Heights, PA, where I lived until 1968, when our family moved to another place in Warminster, PA. (Zip Code 18974)
My mother almost never drank. She did smoke occasionally before marriage, but never while pregnant or when I was growing up. She did not breastfeed me.
I received vaccines for smallpox and polio and perhaps others. I had the following childhood diseases; mumps, measles, and chickenpox. I also had scarlet fever along with frequent tonsillitis, which stopped as I grew older.
My father was a smoker so I was exposed to second hand smoke. Our house was heated with coal, so we were also exposed to coal dust. I lived next to Fischer & Porter, a factory which made flow meters. They contaminated the source of our drinking water with volatile organic compounds: trichloroethylene (TCEs) and perchloroethylene (PCEs). Fischer & Porter (later ABB Engineering) was added to the Superfund Program National Priorities List in 1983. Our housing development was also adjacent (approximately one mile away) to Johnsville Naval Air Station, declared a Superfund site in 1989. This facility contaminated local water sources near us with TCEs, PCEs, PCBs, and PFAs. The elementary school I attended, was across the street from this factory.
I was an avid reader and also enjoyed outdoor activities: biking, walking, playing. I was thin for most of my life until I reached menopause. My adult height was 5’ 6”. We ate a healthy diet I think, partly because  my mother was an excellent cook. Every dinner was balanced with either meat or fish, a carb, and a vegetable. I  loved candy and used my weekly allowance to buy candy, books, and comic books.
Section II – Adolescent years – 10 – 13
Think about potential differences and similarities, including use of alcohol, tobacco, childhood illnesses, use of make-up, body compositions, whether you attended the same school, sports you played, favorite foods, emotional trauma, possible chemical exposures, part-time jobs you might have had, how you spent your summer vacations. Body composition, favorite drinks,  age at menarche if known, medical or dental treatments, viral infections, like mono, shingles etc. Neighborhood you lived, and proximity to factories of any kind, including power plants. Difficulties sleeping, liking for fast food, Overall energy and activity level, hobbies, ways to spend free time. Did your home use well water or public drinking water.
From ages 10-13, I was in the same house in Warminster Heights and attended the same school. At around age 13 I started using cosmetics.   At this age, I did not smoke or use alcohol.  In fact I never smoked. Summer vacations consisted of day trips to the New Jersey Shore where we spent most of the time at the beach.
I had my first period at age 14 which was quite irregular at first, missing often one or more months. During this time I still lived near the factory and Naval Air Station and was still exposed to secondhand smoke and coal. I never had shingles or mono.  I continued to like reading and lots of outdoor play in my spare time.
Section III – Teen years – 13 – 19
Think about potential differences and similarities, including the use of birth control, alcohol, tobacco, legal and illegal drugs (including marijuana, cocaine, etc), Tattoos, and if so approximate size, and colors used. Well or public water at home. Part time jobs. Teen-age acne and whether medications used to control it. Colleges attended and location of. Body  composition, illnesses, including viral such as mono, herpes simplex (cold sores), medications. Medical/dental treatments. Use of cosmetics, hair straighteners, hair dyes, nail polishes. Food preferences – red meat, grilled food fried, vegetables, candy.
I did not drink at all until college, and then very rarely. I did not have tattoos. I  continued to live in Warminster Heights, next to Fischer & Porter factory but was now attending high school. At age 18, I started college in Philadelphia (La Salle University), commuting each day from my home. I recall my health as being good other than the common cold, and rarely had the flu.
By this time I was using cosmetics, including nail polish. I never dyed or straightened my hair. I had an occasional cavity but never had oral surgery. While my mother continued to provide healthy meals, I often liked to indulge in snack food, pizza and candy.
Section IV – Adulthood
Think about potential differences and similarities, including your occupations, married vs. single, use of birth control, hormone replacement therapy, including oral and patches, working night or day shifts, physical area of the country where you lived and how long in any one place. Number of children, if any. Months breast fed, if applicable. Period interruption during breast feeding. Tattoos and/or breast implants, and if so provide some level of detail including material used for breast implants. Surgeries including breast biopsies. Personal stress and level of. Hair dyes and straighteners. Use of cosmetics/nail polishes. Body composition and exercise. Chemical exposures at work/at home/in the surrounding environment. Supplements, including vitamins, if any. Food preferences – red meat, grilled food fried, vegetables, candy. Any family members diagnosed with other types of cancers.
In adulthood, I moved to New Brunswick, NJ to pursue graduate work at Rutgers University. I was a Teaching Assistant. I then earned  my Ph.D., and was an Assistant Professor at Rutgers. At age 35, I moved to Frostburg, MD to teach at Frostburg State University, eventually becoming a Full Professor of English. I lived near sources of pollution coming from pharmaceutical firms in New Jersey and oil refineries in northern New Jersey. Frostburg is an old coal mining town and near a paper mill which emitted pollutants until it shut down. In the 1990s, our water source became a nearby reservoir, which is tested regularly and which shows safe levels of any contaminants—by EPA standards, at least. I often worked long hours, more than 40 hours per week.
I did use birth control. I used oral contraceptives for several (4-5) years, never married and never had children.
I used cosmetics, but over time their use became more infrequent. (Lipstick, mascara). I never dyed my hair but would get a perm regularly (every 2-3) months and still do.
I never smoked. I did not use any illegal drugs (only marijuana, very rarely) and took no prescription drugs until my 50s. I did not use hormone replacement therapy.  I drank wine.
I was diagnosed with exercise-induced asthma at age 55 and use an inhaler as needed (rarely). At age 40, my first mammogram showed a tumor (benign), which was removed. I had fibrocystic tissue in my breasts.
I exercised  regularly and would walk every day for approximately 30 minutes. My diet was healthy. I was a vegetarian for some years, then moved to a plant-based diet that allowed some fish and lean meat. I remained thin, but I gained weight after menopause.
I remain in reasonably good health at age 70—no major illnesses other than arthritis and resultant back problems.
Below is the comprehensive list of topics I am interested in the partipants addressing, where applicable. I have tried to capture these topics  in the descriptions above. It is also possible I have overlooked some thought provoking areas, so please amend as necessary and consider this a work in progress.
Use of cosmetics, including lipstick, nail polish, disposable contacts, hair dyes and straighteners.
Medications including birth control, antibiotics, hormone replacement, including oral and patch.
Food preferences including red meats/grilled/fried/raw/organic/green teas/colas/fruits and veggies
Exercise
Body composition – chubby/thin/athletic/metabolism
Illnesses – including viral infections like mono, shingles, cold sores, extended use of medications
Alcohol use – including binge drinking/one or more glasses per day
Number of children and mother’s age at births
Gender of children if any
Number of months breast feeding if applicable and impact, if any, on period
Tattoos/breast implants – including location, color and size of Tattoos, material used for breast implant
Chemical exposures via air/water/employment/leisure even if only surmised.
Type of work, including night or day shift
Personal Stress, married/divorced/children with illness/sick spouse or parent/Bad job situation
Medical/Dental Treatments, including excessive fillings/sealants/implants
Area of country where lived the longest, with special interest in refineries/chemical plants/dumps/incinerators/power plants/dry cleaning facilities/industrial area
Use of Teflon for cooking
Use of plastics in microwave
Eats out frequently/fast food/microwave popcorn
Family history of breast cancer
Water sources including public/private well/ filtered at tap/bottled water
Marijuana use
Tobacco smoking, including second hand
Illegal drug use
Hobbies – Yoga, music, reading, sports, etc
Age at cancer diagnosis
Sub-type of breast cancer, any other types of cancer, including skin.

I don’t recall at exactly what age, but as a teenager I started to smoke cigarettes. I also started to consume alcohol in high school. I would say maybe 3 – 4 drinks a week. I attended Archbishop Wood High School for Girls in Warminster. Upon graduating high school I went to work at Fischer & Porter, the factory I mentioned previously.  (This was 1968). At age 18. I would say I was quite healthy with very few medical conditions besides the common cold and flu.
I continued to use cosmetics, including nail polish, but I did not dye or straighten my hair. I never had oral surgery but had a handful of cavities. My mother continued to provide healthy meals, but as a teenager I liked snack food, pizza and candy.
Section IV – Adulthood
Think about potential differences and similarities, including your occupations, married vs. single, use of birth control, hormone replacement therapy, including oral and patches, working night or day shifts, physical area of the country where you lived and how long in any one place. Number of children, if any. Months breast fed, if applicable. Period interruption during breast feeding. Tattoos and/or breast implants, and if so provide some level of detail including material used for breast implants. Surgeries including breast biopsies. Personal stress and level of. Food preferences – red meat, grilled food fried, vegetables, candy. Any family members diagnosed with other types of cancers.
As an adult I continued to live in Warminster. I married at age 23 and my husband and I moved to Horsham, PA for a few years.  This township also had water contaminants from the Willow Grove Naval Air Station. We moved back to Warminster around 1976 where my husband and I bought a house. I am currently still living there.
I continued throughout this time to work at Fischer & Porter, where I held many positions. I began as a file clerk, moved on to draftsman, and finally became a Manufacturing Engineer. In the 1980s, Fischer & Porter had been declared a Superfund site, and the water was treated to remove contaminants and regularly tested. I worked long hours.
I used birth control, primarily oral contraceptives for many years and do not have children.
I liked to dye my hair. I also decided to stop smoking in my early 20s. I did not use hormone replacement therapy. I like to drink wine, perhaps 5 – 7 glasses per week.
My childhood asthma returned, and I had to use a steroidal inhaler daily for several years. The asthma finally went away. I was diagnosed with fibrocystic tissue in my breasts.
I exercised regularly often going to the gym 3-4 times a week and often walked. My diet continued to be quite healthy but allowed some fish and lean meat. I liked red meat but mostly ate chicken or fish, lots of salads. I remained thin.
